sources.title: Republic of Palau Public Law (RPPL) No. 11-11, which repeals and replaces Chapter 12 of Title 40 of the Palau National Code: the Palau Goods and Services Tax (PGST) — § 1211 (10 % on a taxable supply and on a supply of imported services, 0 % on a zero-rated supply), § 1212 (zero-rated supplies), § 1213 (the supply of financial services is exempt), § 1214 (10 % on a taxable import, payable at the time of import), § 1241 (input tax credit), § 1261 (net PGST payable for a PGST period = (A + B) - C), § 1262 (an excess of credit is carried forward, and refunded on written application), § 1281 (a return for each PGST period within thirty days after its end), § 1282 (payment by the due date of the return) and the definition of a PGST period as a calendar month
sources.publisher: Bureau of Revenue and Taxation (BRT), Ministry of Finance, Republic of Palau

sources.title: Palau Goods and Services Tax Regulations (as of 2 July 2023): § 312 — the PGST payable on imported services is outside the formula of § 1261 when the registered person uses the services wholly to make taxable supplies, and no recipient-created invoice is prepared in that case; § 401 — apportionment of input tax credits for acquisitions made partly to make taxable supplies
sources.publisher: Bureau of Revenue and Taxation (BRT), Ministry of Finance, Republic of Palau

sources.title: Form Tax 500, Palau Goods & Services Monthly Tax Return (revised 30 July 2022) and its instructions: lines A to C (business outputs), E to H (business inputs), J and K (imported services subject to the reverse charge rules), L and M (business capital assets), N to P (net PGST payable or creditable = N - O), each with an amount excluding PGST in column 1 and the PGST in column 2; the return and the payment are due on or before the thirtieth day of the month following the PGST period; a negative line P is a credit carried forward to the following period
sources.publisher: Bureau of Revenue and Taxation (BRT), Ministry of Finance, Republic of Palau

sources.title: PGST — Input Tax Credit, Tax Returns, Record-keeping: what a creditable acquisition is (a taxable supply by another registered person, a supply of imported services, a taxable import), the documents that support the credit (PGST invoice, customs documentation, recipient-created invoice for imported services, debit or credit note), the monthly self-assessed return lodged by the thirtieth day of the following month and the three-year retention of records
sources.publisher: Bureau of Revenue and Taxation (BRT), Ministry of Finance, Republic of Palau

sources.title: PGST — Types of supplies: the taxable supplies (goods, services, utilities, telecommunications, leases and licences), the list of zero-rated supplies (exports, aircraft and ship stores, international transport and telecommunications, prescription medicine supplied to a licensed pharmacy, clinic or hospital, and the others) and the exempt supplies (financial services)
sources.publisher: Bureau of Revenue and Taxation (BRT), Ministry of Finance, Republic of Palau

sources.title: PGST — Calculating your supplies: registration is compulsory above USD 300,000 of average taxable supplies (the current projected year and the three previous years, divided by four), within seven days of exceeding the threshold; a holder of a Foreign Investment Approval Certificate registers whatever the turnover
sources.publisher: Bureau of Revenue and Taxation (BRT), Ministry of Finance, Republic of Palau

sources.title: Taxpayer calendar for the year 2023: the PGST return of a month is due on the 30th of the month after the PGST period (the January 2023 return on 2 March, thirty days after the end of the period), and a due date that falls on a weekend or a public holiday moves to the next working day
sources.publisher: Bureau of Revenue and Taxation (BRT), Ministry of Finance, Republic of Palau

charts.name: Palau reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: There is no legal chart of accounts in the texts read for Palau: no text found prescribes one, nor the layout of the financial statements. This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of the IAS 1-style statements below (expenses by nature), with the accounts a Palau trading company keeps — PGST output and input tax, import PGST owed at the time of import, wages and salary tax withheld, social security contributions and other taxes payable.

numbering.legal_reference: A PGST invoice must carry the particulars § 1271 of the Act lists; no text read says how invoices are numbered. `sequential` and the number format are conventions of this pack and not rules of the law.

tax_point.legal_reference: Act § 1232 sets the time of supply and § 1211(c) the time the liability arises; the pack does not model the rules of § 1232 and takes the invoice date as the tax point. That is a simplification, recorded in the README.

einvoicing.legal_reference: No structured e-invoice standard, Peppol profile or clearance system of the BRT was found in the texts read; the returns are filed on the Tax 500 form with the Tax Filing App of the Bureau. `obligation` is `none` for want of a text, not on a finding that none exists.
